questions.explanation: Option C was the common wrong answer. The report says many candidates thought gravitational field strength is equivalent to the acceleration of free fall and chose C, and that many confused the descriptions of weight and gravitational field strength. The statement about field strength in C is true, but the statement about weight is not: weight is not a force per unit mass. Weight is the gravitational force on an object, measured in newtons. Gravitational field strength is the gravitational force per unit mass, in N/kg. Answer: D. Check the units to see which is which.

Most candidates used an incorrect rearrangement of the moment equation. Moment = force × distance, so the minimum force is moment divided by distance, not distance divided by moment. Convert the distance first: 30 cm = 0.30 m. F = 25 / 0.30 = 83 N: D. The wrong route, 30 / 25 = 1.2, is option A. Divide the quantity you are asked for by the one you are given, and check that the answer comes out in newtons.

The report found answers spread across all four options, suggesting many candidates guessed. Work out what each part of the flask does. The vacuum between the walls has no particles, so there is nothing to carry energy by conduction or convection. A vacuum does not stop radiation. That is the job of the silvered walls, which are poor emitters and good reflectors. So the vacuum itself reduces conduction and convection only: B.

Option D was the common wrong answer. Most candidates used the correct rearrangement, λ = v / f, but did not take the prefix kilo into account. 1500 / 26 = 58 gives 58 m, which is option D. 26 kHz is 26 000 Hz, so λ = 1500 / 26 000 = 0.058 m = 58 mm: B. Convert the prefix before you divide.

Although most candidates knew the order of the colours in the visible spectrum, the report says the majority of those could not list them in order of decreasing frequency. Option A, red, yellow, blue, runs the wrong way: that is increasing frequency. Violet has the highest frequency in the visible spectrum and red the lowest, so violet, orange, red is in decreasing order: D.

Option D was the common wrong answer. The report says many candidates thought ultrasound is a transverse wave. All sound waves are longitudinal, whatever the frequency. A is the only row that works: 3.0 kHz is audible and 30 kHz is above the upper limit of human hearing. B and C fail because both waves travel in air at the same speed, so the higher frequency has the shorter wavelength. Answer: A.

The report found answers spread across all four options, suggesting many candidates guessed. Induced magnetism is when a piece of magnetic material, such as soft iron, becomes a magnet only because it is in a magnetic field. B, C and D all use that. A compass needle is already a permanent magnet. It lines up with the Earth's field, but the field is not magnetising it. So A is the one that is not an example.

Options B and D were the common wrong answers. The report says most candidates did not recall the equation for the energy transferred by the lamp. Energy = power × time = 24 × 20 = 480 J: C. Option B, 240 J, is p.d. × time (12 × 20). Option D, about 5800 J, is p.d. × power × time (12 × 24 × 20 = 5760). These are the two wrong equations the report names. The power of 24 W already includes the p.d., so p.d. does not appear again.

Options B and C were the common wrong answers. The report says most candidates suggested a change that would increase the resistance and so decrease the current. The question asks for an increase in current, which needs a decrease in resistance. A second identical wire in parallel halves the resistance: A. A second wire in series, a thinner wire and a longer wire all raise the resistance. Read increase or decrease again before you choose.

Most candidates knew that a fuse protects the wiring from overheating. Many also thought it protects people from an electric shock, and chose A. A fuse melts when the current goes above its rating, and it does not decide whether a person is safe. Protection from shock comes from insulation and earthing. Only student 1 is correct: C.

Most candidates determined that the force is either to the right or to the left. Many chose A, thinking that because something had been reversed the force would reverse. Two things were reversed here, the magnetic field and the connections to the power supply, so the direction of the force is unchanged. Reversing the current alone, or the field alone, would reverse the force. Reversing both brings it back to the right: B.

Many candidates chose B, believing an alpha particle has a charge of −2. It is +2. An alpha particle is a helium nucleus, two protons and two neutrons, so it contains two neutrons: A. It is also strongly ionising and not very penetrating, which rules out C and D.

Many candidates chose D. The report says most recalled that light-years is a possible unit for the diameter of the Milky Way, but many thought the diameter was 100 million light-years instead of 100 thousand. The syllabus gives the diameter of the Milky Way as approximately 100 000 light-years. A galaxy is far too large to be measured in kilometres, so the choice is between C and D: C.
